subject: Re: Sponsorship addendum — speaking credit trade and logo placement
messages:
From: Lara Quinn <lara@cloudburstevents.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: sponsorships@cloudburstevents.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — Sponsorship package and speaker credit availability

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for your interest in SummitCloud '26. I put together the standard bronze + speaking credit package you asked about — attached is the baseline package with what we can offer for booth placement, logo tiers, and one 20-minute breakout slot.

A few notes up front: our standard bronze includes a 6'x10' demo table (inline), logo on the website at tier C, and one sponsor listing in the printed guide. Speaking slots are tightly managed; the 20-minute breakout is typically non-promoted (no conference-wide promo) unless you upgrade to silver.

If you want more visibility — prime logo placement on the stage banner, promoted email to attendees, or a keynote adjacent speaking slot — we can add those a la carte. I've highlighted feasible add-ons in the attached PDF.

Would you like me to mark up a custom addendum that trades a partial speaking upgrade for a logo placement bump?

Best,
Lara
Sponsorships Manager
CloudBurst Events
[Attachment: Sponsorship_Addendum_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Quinn <lara@cloudburstevents.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — Sponsorship package and speaker credit availability

Hi Lara,

Thanks — I reviewed the PDF. Quick priorities for us: 1) stronger logo placement on the main stage banner (we need visibility during keynotes), 2) promotion of our sponsored breakout in the mobile app/email, and 3) the ability to trade speaking time for visibility (we can accept a shorter 12-minute slot if it gains stage logo placement and an email mention).

Kimberly, Camila — looping you in for ops/AV needs and to confirm booth footprint.

Markus
Head of Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

Markus — appreciate the clear asks. I sketched a focused addendum: trade the 20-minute breakout for a promoted 12-minute stage adjacent slot (mid-morning) plus Tier B logo placement on the main stage scrim and a promoted push in the summit app. The price delta is modest — I noted it on page 2 of the attached addendum.

Two operational things: 1) stage adjacent slots are assigned late in the program process; we can reserve one in writing but final time is TBD, 2) Booth footprint for the upgraded package becomes a 10'x10' island (corner preference, subject to floorplan).

I attached a revised addendum and the latest floorplan overlay (A_v4). If that works I can send a DocuSign today.

Quick ops notes — 10'x10' island is fine. AV list: we need a podium mic, a lav for the speaker, HDMI + adapter, confidence monitor, and 20 minutes of soundcheck time in the morning. Can Lara confirm that the promoted push in the app includes a session spotlight (one graphic + 150-word blurb) and that we get one pre-conference email mention (sponsor highlight)? Also, confirm whether the corner island placement precludes a demo table in front of the booth (we typically staff with two people and want a demo surface).

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Field Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Lara Quinn <lara@cloudburstevents.com>

Thanks all — confirmed: the promoted app push includes a session spotlight (graphic + 150-word blurb) and one pre-conference sponsor email to registered attendees. The corner island still allows a 3' demo counter to run along the aisle; I'll note that in the ops sheet.

About AV: podium mic + lav, HDMI + adapters, and a confidence monitor are all on the standard tech rider for the stage adjacent slot. We'll reserve a 15-minute soundcheck window — if you need 20 minutes we'll try to prioritize.

I also flagged two minor contract tweaks in the addendum: 1) a clause clarifying logo bleed area for the scrim (to avoid last-minute cropping), and 2) a force majeure carve-out specific to venue HVAC work. If those look good I'll push the DocuSign.

Lara

Markus
